The **1992 Summer Olympics** ([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): _Juegos Olímpicos de Verano de 1992_, [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalan_language "Catalan language"): _Jocs Olímpics d'estiu de 1992_), officially the **Games of the XXV Olympiad** ([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): _Juegos de la XXV Olimpiada_, [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalan_language "Catalan language"): _Jocs de la XXV Olimpíada_) and officially branded as **Barcelona '92**, were an international [multi-sport event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-sport_event "Multi-sport event") held from 25 July to 9 August 1992 in [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"), Catalonia, Spain. Beginning in 1994, the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") decided to hold the Summer and Winter Olympics in alternating even-numbered years. The 1992 Summer and Winter Olympics were the last games to be staged in the same year.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-3) These games were the second and last two consecutive Olympic games to be held in Western Europe after the [1992 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Winter_Olympics "1992 Winter Olympics") in Albertville, France, held five months earlier. It is also the second [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") to be held in a Spanish-speaking country, following the [1968 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Summer_Olympics "1968 Summer Olympics") in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City").

The 1992 Games received universal acclaim, with the organisation, volunteers, sportsmanship, and Spanish public being lauded in the international media. Some media[_[weasel words](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Avoid\_weasel\_words "Wikipedia:Avoid weasel words")_] describe the Barcelona Games as one of the best Olympics ever.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Best_ever-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Atlanta_criticism-5) The Games showed a renewed image of a democratic Spain and projected Barcelona and Catalonia to the world. Owing to the Games, the city of Barcelona was remarkably transformed.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-6) All the venues are still active, and the legacy of the 1992 Games was taken as an example for future Olympic events, such as [London 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-7)

The 1992 Summer Games were the first since the [end of the](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War_(1985%E2%80%931991) "Cold War (1985–1991)")[Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), and the first unaffected by boycotts since the [1972 Summer Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics "1972 Summer Olympics").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-8) 1992 was also the first year South Africa [was re-invited to the Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics "South Africa at the 1992 Summer Olympics") by the International Olympic Committee, after a [32-year ban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid-era_South_Africa_and_the_Olympics "Apartheid-era South Africa and the Olympics") from participating in international sport due to [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-9) The [Unified Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_Team_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics "Unified Team at the 1992 Summer Olympics") (made up by the former [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union")[republics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republics_of_the_Soviet_Union "Republics of the Soviet Union") without the [Baltic states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltic_states "Baltic states")) topped the medal table, winning 45 gold and 112 overall medals.

## Host city selection

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1992_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Host city selection")]

Barcelona was the second-largest city in Spain and the capital of the autonomous community of [Catalonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalonia "Catalonia"); it is also the hometown of then-[IOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") president [Juan Antonio Samaranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Antonio_Samaranch "Juan Antonio Samaranch") and the famous European club [FC Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona"). The city was also a host for the [1982 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup "1982 FIFA World Cup"). On 17 October 1986, Barcelona was selected to host the 1992 Summer Olympics over [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam"), which hosted the [1928 games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1928_Summer_Olympics "1928 Summer Olympics"); [Belgrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade"), Yugoslavia; [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham"), United Kingdom; [Brisbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane "Brisbane"), Australia; and [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), France, during the 91st [IOC Session](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOC_Session "IOC Session") in [Lausanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lausanne "Lausanne"), [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-10)[New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi"), India, had announced a bid for the games, but withdrew in March 1986.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-11) With 85 out of 89 members of the IOC voting by secret ballot, Barcelona won a majority of 47 votes. Samaranch abstained from voting. In the same IOC meeting, Albertville, France, won the right to host the [1992 Winter Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Winter_Olympics "1992 Winter Olympics"). Paris and Brisbane would eventually be selected to host the [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics") and [2032 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2032_Summer_Olympics "2032 Summer Olympics") respectively.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-12)

Barcelona had previously bid for the [1936 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936_Summer_Olympics "1936 Summer Olympics") that were ultimately held in [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin"), Germany. As an [anti-fascist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-fascism "Anti-fascism") response against the Games being organized by [Nazi Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany"), the [Government of Catalonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalitat_de_Catalunya "Generalitat de Catalunya") and the newly elected Spanish [Popular Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_Front_(Spain) "Popular Front (Spain)") government advocated for the boycott of the [Spanish Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Spanish_Republic "Second Spanish Republic") to the Berlin Games and the organization of an alternative games in Barcelona, known as the [People's Olympiad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Olympiad "People's Olympiad").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Harrison-1-13) However, the same day of its planned inauguration (19 July), the [Spanish Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Army "Spanish Army") carried out a [coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_coup_of_July_1936 "Spanish coup of July 1936") which led to the [Spanish Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War "Spanish Civil War").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-14)

*   At the innovative opening ceremony, Greek mezzo-soprano [Agnes Baltsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agnes_Baltsa "Agnes Baltsa") sang "Romiossini" as the Olympic flag was paraded around the stadium. [Alfredo Kraus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfredo_Kraus "Alfredo Kraus") later sang the [Olympic Hymn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Hymn "Olympic Hymn") in Catalan, Spanish and French, as the flag was hoisted.
*   The Olympic cauldron was ignited using a flaming arrow, lit from the flame of the [Olympic torch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_flame "Olympic flame"). It was shot by [Paralympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paralympic "Paralympic") archer [Antonio Rebollo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Rebollo "Antonio Rebollo"), who aimed the arrow over the top of the cauldron to ignite the gas emanating from it. The arrow landed outside the stadium.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-16) This unusual method for lighting the cauldron had been carefully designed to avoid any chance of the arrow landing in the stadium if Rebollo missed his target.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-18)
*   South Africa rejoined the Summer Olympics having been banned for its [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid") policy after the [1960 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_Summer_Olympics "1960 Summer Olympics"). The [women's 10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 1992 Summer Olympics – Women's 10,000 metres") event was hotly contested. White South African runner [Elana Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elana_Meyer "Elana Meyer") and black [Ethiopian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Ethiopia at the Summer Olympics") runner [Derartu Tulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derartu_Tulu "Derartu Tulu") (winner) ran hand-in-hand in a victory lap.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-19)
*   Germany sent a unified team having [reunified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_reunification "German reunification") in 1990, the last such team was at the [1964 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics "1964 Summer Olympics").
*   As the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") was [dissolved in 1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collapse_of_the_Soviet_Union "Collapse of the Soviet Union"), the formerly [Soviet-occupied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupation_of_the_Baltic_states "Occupation of the Baltic states") states of [Estonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estonia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Estonia at the Summer Olympics") and [Latvia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Latvia at the Summer Olympics") sent their own teams for the first time since 1936, while [Lithuania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuania_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Lithuania at the Summer Olympics") sent its own team for the first time since 1928. The other former Soviet republics decided to compete together and formed the [Unified Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_Team_at_the_Olympics "Unified Team at the Olympics"), which consisted of present-day [Armenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Armenia at the Summer Olympics"), [Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Azerbaijan at the Summer Olympics"), [Belarus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarus_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Belarus at the Summer Olympics"), [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Georgia at the Summer Olympics"), [Kazakhstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakhstan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Kazakhstan at the Summer Olympics"), [Kyrgyzstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrgyzstan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Kyrgyzstan at the Summer Olympics"), [Moldova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldova_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Moldova at the Summer Olympics"), [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Russia at the Summer Olympics"), [Tajikistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tajikistan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Tajikistan at the Summer Olympics"), [Turkmenistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkmenistan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Turkmenistan at the Summer Olympics"), [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Ukraine at the Summer Olympics"), and [Uzbekistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzbekistan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Uzbekistan at the Summer Olympics"). The Unified Team finished first in the medal standings, edging second-placed [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics "United States at the 1992 Summer Olympics") 112 to 108 in total medals and 45 to 37 in golds.
*   The [separation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakup_of_Yugoslavia "Breakup of Yugoslavia") of the [Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia") led to the Olympic debuts of [Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Croatia at the Summer Olympics"), [Slovenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovenia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Slovenia at the Summer Olympics") and [Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Bosnia and Herzegovina at the Summer Olympics"). Due to [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") sanctions, athletes from the [Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia_and_Montenegro_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Serbia and Montenegro at the Summer Olympics") (consisting of present-day [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") and [Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro")) were not allowed to participate with their own team. However, some individual athletes competed under the Olympic flag as [Independent Olympic Participants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Olympic_Participants_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics "Independent Olympic Participants at the 1992 Summer Olympics"). Serbia would return to the Olympics at the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") and as well as Montenegro on what would be its Olympic debut as separate states.
*   In [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball"), the admittance of NBA players led to the formation of the "[Dream Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_United_States_men's_Olympic_basketball_team "1992 United States men's Olympic basketball team")" of the United States, featuring [Michael Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jordan "Michael Jordan"), [Magic Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_Johnson "Magic Johnson"), [Larry Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Bird "Larry Bird") and other [NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") stars. Prior to 1992, only European and South American professionals were allowed to compete, while the Americans used college players. The Dream Team won the gold medal and was inducted as a unit into the [Basketball Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_Hall_of_Fame "Basketball Hall of Fame") in 2010.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-20)
*   [Fermín Cacho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferm%C3%ADn_Cacho "Fermín Cacho") won the [1,500 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1500_metres "1500 metres") in his home country, earning Spain's first-ever Olympic gold medal in a running event.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-21)
*   [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_at_the_Summer_Olympics "China at the Summer Olympics")[diver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diving_(sport) "Diving (sport)")[Fu Mingxia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fu_Mingxia "Fu Mingxia"), age 13, became one of the youngest Olympic gold medalists of all time.
*   In men's [artistic gymnastics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artistic_gymnastics "Artistic gymnastics"), [Vitaly Scherbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitaly_Scherbo "Vitaly Scherbo") from [Belarus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarus_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Belarus at the Summer Olympics"), (representing the [Unified Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_Team_at_the_Olympics "Unified Team at the Olympics")), won six gold medals, including four in a single day. Scherbo tied [Eric Heiden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Heiden "Eric Heiden")'s record for individual gold medals at a single Olympics, winning five medals in an individual event ([Michael Phelps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Phelps "Michael Phelps") would later equal this record in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics")).
*   In women's artistic gymnastics, [Tatiana Gutsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tatiana_Gutsu "Tatiana Gutsu") took gold in the All-Around competition edging [Shannon Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannon_Miller "Shannon Miller").
*   Russian swimmers (competing for the Unified Team) dominated the men's freestyle events, with [Alexander Popov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Popov_(swimmer) "Alexander Popov (swimmer)") and [Yevgeny Sadovyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yevgeny_Sadovyi "Yevgeny Sadovyi") each winning two events. Sadovyi also won in the relays.
*   [Evelyn Ashford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evelyn_Ashford "Evelyn Ashford") won her fourth Olympic gold medal in the 4×100-metre relay, making her one of only four female athletes to have achieved this in history.
*   The young [Krisztina Egerszegi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krisztina_Egerszegi "Krisztina Egerszegi") of [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Hungary at the Summer Olympics") won three individual swimming gold medals.
*   In women's 200 m [breaststroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breaststroke "Breaststroke"), [Kyoko Iwasaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyoko_Iwasaki "Kyoko Iwasaki") of [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Japan at the Summer Olympics") won a gold medal at the age of 14 years and six days, making her the youngest-ever gold medalist in swimming competitions at the Olympics.
*   [Algerian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algeria "Algeria") athlete [Hassiba Boulmerka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hassiba_Boulmerka "Hassiba Boulmerka"), who was frequently criticized by Muslim groups in Algeria who thought she showed too much of her body when racing, received [death threats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_threat "Death threat")[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-BBC-22) and was forced to move to Europe to train, won the [1,500 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1500_metres "1500 metres"), also holding the [African women's record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_records_in_athletics "African records in athletics") in this distance.
*   After being demonstrated in six previous Summer Olympic Games, [baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball "Baseball") officially became an Olympic sport. [Badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton "Badminton") and women's [judo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judo "Judo") also became part of the Olympic program, while [slalom canoeing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slalom_canoeing "Slalom canoeing") returned to the Games after a 20-year absence.
*   [Roller hockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roller_hockey_(Quad) "Roller hockey (Quad)"), [Basque pelota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basque_pelota "Basque pelota"), and [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taekwondo "Taekwondo") were all demonstrated at the 1992 Summer Olympics.
*   Several of the USA men's volleyball gold medal team from the [1988 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics "1988 Summer Olympics") returned to vie for another medal. In the preliminary round, they lost a controversial match to Japan, sparking them to shave their heads in protest of referees' decision to order a replay of two sets after an apparent U.S. victory. This notably included player [Steve Timmons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Timmons "Steve Timmons"), sacrificing his trademark red [flattop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flattop "Flattop") for the protest. The U.S. team ultimately progressed to the playoffs and won bronze, having lost the semifinals to eventual gold medallists [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_men's_national_volleyball_team "Brazil men's national volleyball team"), who were beginning to build their own dynasty in the sport.
*   [Mike Stulce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Stulce "Mike Stulce") of the United States won the men's [shot put](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shot_put "Shot put"), beating the heavily favored [Werner Günthör](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Werner_G%C3%BCnth%C3%B6r "Werner Günthör") of Switzerland.
*   On the 20th anniversary of the [Munich massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich_massacre "Munich massacre") and the 500th anniversary of the [Alhambra Decree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alhambra_Decree "Alhambra Decree"), [Yael Arad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yael_Arad "Yael Arad") became the first Israeli to win an Olympic medal, winning a silver medal in judo. The next day, [Oren Smadja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oren_Smadja "Oren Smadja") became Israel's first male medalist, winning a bronze in the same sport.
*   [Derek Redmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Redmond "Derek Redmond") of Great Britain tore a hamstring during a 400-meter semi-final heat. As he struggled to finish the race, his father entered the track without credentials and helped him complete the race, to a [standing ovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_ovation "Standing ovation") from the crowd.
*   [Gail Devers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gail_Devers "Gail Devers") came into the 100 meters hurdles as the favorite. Though her Olympic history shows her winning the 100 meters dash twice, the first time earlier in this Olympics, she primarily made her career as a hurdler. And true to form, Devers had a commanding lead in this race until the final hurdle. Devers came up short and hit the hurdle, foot first, hard, knocking her off balance. She stumbled toward the finish line, falling on the last step, but still finished fifth, .001 out of fourth place. [Paraskevi Patoulidou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraskevi_Patoulidou "Paraskevi Patoulidou") of Greece won the gold medal to even her own disbelief, dropping to her knees on the track when she realized she had won.
*   [Jennifer Capriati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Capriati "Jennifer Capriati") won the singles tennis competition at the age of 16. She had previously earned a spot in the semifinals of two grand slams at the age of 14.
*   Two gold medals were awarded in solo synchronized swimming after a judge inadvertently entered the score of "8.7" instead of the intended "9.7" in the computerized scoring system for one of [Sylvie Fréchette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvie_Fr%C3%A9chette "Sylvie Fréchette")'s figures. This error ultimately placed Fréchette second, leaving [Kristen Babb-Sprague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Babb-Sprague "Kristen Babb-Sprague") for the gold medal. Following an appeal, [FINA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FINA "FINA") awarded Fréchette a gold medal, replacing her silver medal and leaving the two swimmers both with gold.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-23)
*   Indonesia won its first-ever gold medal after winning a silver at [1988 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics "1988 Summer Olympics"). [Susi Susanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susi_Susanti "Susi Susanti") won the gold in [badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton "Badminton") women's singles after defeating [Bang Soo-hyun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bang_Soo-hyun "Bang Soo-hyun") in the final round. [Alan Budikusuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Budikusuma "Alan Budikusuma") won the badminton men's singles competition, earning a second gold medal for Indonesia. Several years later, both players married and they received the nickname golden couple or Olympic couple.

    *   [Palau de la Metal·lúrgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palau_de_la_Metal%C2%B7l%C3%BArgia "Palau de la Metal·lúrgia") – fencing, modern pentathlon (fencing)
    *   [Pavelló de l'Espanya Industrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavell%C3%B3_de_l'Espanya_Industrial "Pavelló de l'Espanya Industrial") – weightlifting

The **1992 Summer Olympics** ([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): _Juegos Olímpicos de Verano de 1992_, [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalan_language "Catalan language"): _Jocs Olímpics d'estiu de 1992_), officially the **Games of the XXV Olympiad** ([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): _Juegos de la XXV Olimpiada_, [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalan_language "Catalan language"): _Jocs de la XXV Olimpíada_) and officially branded as **Barcelona '92**, were an international [multi-sport event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-sport_event "Multi-sport event") held from 25 July to 9 August 1992 in [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"), Catalonia, Spain. Beginning in 1994, the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") decided to hold the Summer and Winter Olympics in alternating even-numbered years. The 1992 Summer and Winter Olympics were the last games to be staged in the same year.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-3) These games were the second and last two consecutive Olympic games to be held in Western Europe after the [1992 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Winter_Olympics "1992 Winter Olympics") in Albertville, France, held five months earlier. It is also the second [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") to be held in a Spanish-speaking country, following the [1968 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Summer_Olympics "1968 Summer Olympics") in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City").

The 1992 Games received universal acclaim, with the organisation, volunteers, sportsmanship, and Spanish public being lauded in the international media. Some media[_[weasel words](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Avoid\_weasel\_words "Wikipedia:Avoid weasel words")_] describe the Barcelona Games as one of the best Olympics ever.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Best_ever-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Atlanta_criticism-5) The Games showed a renewed image of a democratic Spain and projected Barcelona and Catalonia to the world. Owing to the Games, the city of Barcelona was remarkably transformed.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-6) All the venues are still active, and the legacy of the 1992 Games was taken as an example for future Olympic events, such as [London 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-7)

The 1992 Summer Games were the first since the [end of the](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War_(1985%E2%80%931991) "Cold War (1985–1991)")[Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), and the first unaffected by boycotts since the [1972 Summer Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics "1972 Summer Olympics").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-8) 1992 was also the first year South Africa [was re-invited to the Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics "South Africa at the 1992 Summer Olympics") by the International Olympic Committee, after a [32-year ban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid-era_South_Africa_and_the_Olympics "Apartheid-era South Africa and the Olympics") from participating in international sport due to [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-9) The [Unified Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_Team_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics "Unified Team at the 1992 Summer Olympics") (made up by the former [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union")[republics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republics_of_the_Soviet_Union "Republics of the Soviet Union") without the [Baltic states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltic_states "Baltic states")) topped the medal table, winning 45 gold and 112 overall medals.

## Host city selection

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1992_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Host city selection")]

Barcelona was the second-largest city in Spain and the capital of the autonomous community of [Catalonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalonia "Catalonia"); it is also the hometown of then-[IOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") president [Juan Antonio Samaranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Antonio_Samaranch "Juan Antonio Samaranch") and the famous European club [FC Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona"). The city was also a host for the [1982 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup "1982 FIFA World Cup"). On 17 October 1986, Barcelona was selected to host the 1992 Summer Olympics over [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam"), which hosted the [1928 games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1928_Summer_Olympics "1928 Summer Olympics"); [Belgrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade"), Yugoslavia; [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham"), United Kingdom; [Brisbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane "Brisbane"), Australia; and [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), France, during the 91st [IOC Session](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOC_Session "IOC Session") in [Lausanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lausanne "Lausanne"), [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-10)[New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi"), India, had announced a bid for the games, but withdrew in March 1986.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-11) With 85 out of 89 members of the IOC voting by secret ballot, Barcelona won a majority of 47 votes. Samaranch abstained from voting. In the same IOC meeting, Albertville, France, won the right to host the [1992 Winter Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Winter_Olympics "1992 Winter Olympics"). Paris and Brisbane would eventually be selected to host the [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics") and [2032 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2032_Summer_Olympics "2032 Summer Olympics") respectively.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-12)

Barcelona had previously bid for the [1936 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936_Summer_Olympics "1936 Summer Olympics") that were ultimately held in [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin"), Germany. As an [anti-fascist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-fascism "Anti-fascism") response against the Games being organized by [Nazi Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany"), the [Government of Catalonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalitat_de_Catalunya "Generalitat de Catalunya") and the newly elected Spanish [Popular Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_Front_(Spain) "Popular Front (Spain)") government advocated for the boycott of the [Spanish Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Spanish_Republic "Second Spanish Republic") to the Berlin Games and the organization of an alternative games in Barcelona, known as the [People's Olympiad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Olympiad "People's Olympiad").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-Harrison-1-13) However, the same day of its planned inauguration (19 July), the [Spanish Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Army "Spanish Army") carried out a [coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_coup_of_July_1936 "Spanish coup of July 1936") which led to the [Spanish Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War "Spanish Civil War").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-14)

[David Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Robinson_(basketball) "David Robinson (basketball)") shoots a free throw to help secure the gold medal for the [United States "Dream Team".](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_United_States_men's_Olympic_basketball_team "1992 United States men's Olympic basketball team")

*   At the innovative opening ceremony, Greek mezzo-soprano [Agnes Baltsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agnes_Baltsa "Agnes Baltsa") sang "Romiossini" as the Olympic flag was paraded around the stadium. [Alfredo Kraus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfredo_Kraus "Alfredo Kraus") later sang the [Olympic Hymn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Hymn "Olympic Hymn") in Catalan, Spanish and French, as the flag was hoisted.
*   The Olympic cauldron was ignited using a flaming arrow, lit from the flame of the [Olympic torch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_flame "Olympic flame"). It was shot by [Paralympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paralympic "Paralympic") archer [Antonio Rebollo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Rebollo "Antonio Rebollo"), who aimed the arrow over the top of the cauldron to ignite the gas emanating from it. The arrow landed outside the stadium.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-16) This unusual method for lighting the cauldron had been carefully designed to avoid any chance of the arrow landing in the stadium if Rebollo missed his target.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-18)
*   South Africa rejoined the Summer Olympics having been banned for its [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid") policy after the [1960 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_Summer_Olympics "1960 Summer Olympics"). The [women's 10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 1992 Summer Olympics – Women's 10,000 metres") event was hotly contested. White South African runner [Elana Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elana_Meyer "Elana Meyer") and black [Ethiopian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Ethiopia at the Summer Olympics") runner [Derartu Tulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derartu_Tulu "Derartu Tulu") (winner) ran hand-in-hand in a victory lap.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-19)
*   Germany sent a unified team having [reunified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_reunification "German reunification") in 1990, the last such team was at the [1964 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics "1964 Summer Olympics").
*   As the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") was [dissolved in 1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collapse_of_the_Soviet_Union "Collapse of the Soviet Union"), the formerly [Soviet-occupied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupation_of_the_Baltic_states "Occupation of the Baltic states") states of [Estonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estonia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Estonia at the Summer Olympics") and [Latvia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Latvia at the Summer Olympics") sent their own teams for the first time since 1936, while [Lithuania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuania_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Lithuania at the Summer Olympics") sent its own team for the first time since 1928. The other former Soviet republics decided to compete together and formed the [Unified Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_Team_at_the_Olympics "Unified Team at the Olympics"), which consisted of present-day [Armenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Armenia at the Summer Olympics"), [Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Azerbaijan at the Summer Olympics"), [Belarus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarus_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Belarus at the Summer Olympics"), [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Georgia at the Summer Olympics"), [Kazakhstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakhstan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Kazakhstan at the Summer Olympics"), [Kyrgyzstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrgyzstan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Kyrgyzstan at the Summer Olympics"), [Moldova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldova_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Moldova at the Summer Olympics"), [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Russia at the Summer Olympics"), [Tajikistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tajikistan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Tajikistan at the Summer Olympics"), [Turkmenistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkmenistan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Turkmenistan at the Summer Olympics"), [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Ukraine at the Summer Olympics"), and [Uzbekistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzbekistan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Uzbekistan at the Summer Olympics"). The Unified Team finished first in the medal standings, edging second-placed [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics "United States at the 1992 Summer Olympics") 112 to 108 in total medals and 45 to 37 in golds.
*   The [separation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakup_of_Yugoslavia "Breakup of Yugoslavia") of the [Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia") led to the Olympic debuts of [Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Croatia at the Summer Olympics"), [Slovenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovenia_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Slovenia at the Summer Olympics") and [Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Bosnia and Herzegovina at the Summer Olympics"). Due to [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") sanctions, athletes from the [Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia_and_Montenegro_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Serbia and Montenegro at the Summer Olympics") (consisting of present-day [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") and [Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro")) were not allowed to participate with their own team. However, some individual athletes competed under the Olympic flag as [Independent Olympic Participants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Olympic_Participants_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics "Independent Olympic Participants at the 1992 Summer Olympics"). Serbia would return to the Olympics at the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") and as well as Montenegro on what would be its Olympic debut as separate states.
*   In [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball"), the admittance of NBA players led to the formation of the "[Dream Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_United_States_men's_Olympic_basketball_team "1992 United States men's Olympic basketball team")" of the United States, featuring [Michael Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jordan "Michael Jordan"), [Magic Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_Johnson "Magic Johnson"), [Larry Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Bird "Larry Bird") and other [NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") stars. Prior to 1992, only European and South American professionals were allowed to compete, while the Americans used college players. The Dream Team won the gold medal and was inducted as a unit into the [Basketball Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_Hall_of_Fame "Basketball Hall of Fame") in 2010.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-20)
*   [Fermín Cacho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferm%C3%ADn_Cacho "Fermín Cacho") won the [1,500 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1500_metres "1500 metres") in his home country, earning Spain's first-ever Olympic gold medal in a running event.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-21)
*   [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_at_the_Summer_Olympics "China at the Summer Olympics")[diver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diving_(sport) "Diving (sport)")[Fu Mingxia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fu_Mingxia "Fu Mingxia"), age 13, became one of the youngest Olympic gold medalists of all time.
*   In men's [artistic gymnastics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artistic_gymnastics "Artistic gymnastics"), [Vitaly Scherbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitaly_Scherbo "Vitaly Scherbo") from [Belarus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarus_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Belarus at the Summer Olympics"), (representing the [Unified Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_Team_at_the_Olympics "Unified Team at the Olympics")), won six gold medals, including four in a single day. Scherbo tied [Eric Heiden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Heiden "Eric Heiden")'s record for individual gold medals at a single Olympics, winning five medals in an individual event ([Michael Phelps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Phelps "Michael Phelps") would later equal this record in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics")).
*   In women's artistic gymnastics, [Tatiana Gutsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tatiana_Gutsu "Tatiana Gutsu") took gold in the All-Around competition edging [Shannon Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannon_Miller "Shannon Miller").
*   Russian swimmers (competing for the Unified Team) dominated the men's freestyle events, with [Alexander Popov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Popov_(swimmer) "Alexander Popov (swimmer)") and [Yevgeny Sadovyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yevgeny_Sadovyi "Yevgeny Sadovyi") each winning two events. Sadovyi also won in the relays.
*   [Evelyn Ashford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evelyn_Ashford "Evelyn Ashford") won her fourth Olympic gold medal in the 4×100-metre relay, making her one of only four female athletes to have achieved this in history.
*   The young [Krisztina Egerszegi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krisztina_Egerszegi "Krisztina Egerszegi") of [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Hungary at the Summer Olympics") won three individual swimming gold medals.
*   In women's 200 m [breaststroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breaststroke "Breaststroke"), [Kyoko Iwasaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyoko_Iwasaki "Kyoko Iwasaki") of [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Japan at the Summer Olympics") won a gold medal at the age of 14 years and six days, making her the youngest-ever gold medalist in swimming competitions at the Olympics.
*   [Algerian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algeria "Algeria") athlete [Hassiba Boulmerka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hassiba_Boulmerka "Hassiba Boulmerka"), who was frequently criticized by Muslim groups in Algeria who thought she showed too much of her body when racing, received [death threats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_threat "Death threat")[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-BBC-22) and was forced to move to Europe to train, won the [1,500 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1500_metres "1500 metres"), also holding the [African women's record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_records_in_athletics "African records in athletics") in this distance.
*   After being demonstrated in six previous Summer Olympic Games, [baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball "Baseball") officially became an Olympic sport. [Badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton "Badminton") and women's [judo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judo "Judo") also became part of the Olympic program, while [slalom canoeing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slalom_canoeing "Slalom canoeing") returned to the Games after a 20-year absence.
*   [Roller hockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roller_hockey_(Quad) "Roller hockey (Quad)"), [Basque pelota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basque_pelota "Basque pelota"), and [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taekwondo "Taekwondo") were all demonstrated at the 1992 Summer Olympics.
*   Several of the USA men's volleyball gold medal team from the [1988 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics "1988 Summer Olympics") returned to vie for another medal. In the preliminary round, they lost a controversial match to Japan, sparking them to shave their heads in protest of referees' decision to order a replay of two sets after an apparent U.S. victory. This notably included player [Steve Timmons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Timmons "Steve Timmons"), sacrificing his trademark red [flattop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flattop "Flattop") for the protest. The U.S. team ultimately progressed to the playoffs and won bronze, having lost the semifinals to eventual gold medallists [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_men's_national_volleyball_team "Brazil men's national volleyball team"), who were beginning to build their own dynasty in the sport.
*   [Mike Stulce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Stulce "Mike Stulce") of the United States won the men's [shot put](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shot_put "Shot put"), beating the heavily favored [Werner Günthör](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Werner_G%C3%BCnth%C3%B6r "Werner Günthör") of Switzerland.
*   On the 20th anniversary of the [Munich massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich_massacre "Munich massacre") and the 500th anniversary of the [Alhambra Decree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alhambra_Decree "Alhambra Decree"), [Yael Arad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yael_Arad "Yael Arad") became the first Israeli to win an Olympic medal, winning a silver medal in judo. The next day, [Oren Smadja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oren_Smadja "Oren Smadja") became Israel's first male medalist, winning a bronze in the same sport.
*   [Derek Redmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Redmond "Derek Redmond") of Great Britain tore a hamstring during a 400-meter semi-final heat. As he struggled to finish the race, his father entered the track without credentials and helped him complete the race, to a [standing ovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_ovation "Standing ovation") from the crowd.
*   [Gail Devers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gail_Devers "Gail Devers") came into the 100 meters hurdles as the favorite. Though her Olympic history shows her winning the 100 meters dash twice, the first time earlier in this Olympics, she primarily made her career as a hurdler. And true to form, Devers had a commanding lead in this race until the final hurdle. Devers came up short and hit the hurdle, foot first, hard, knocking her off balance. She stumbled toward the finish line, falling on the last step, but still finished fifth, .001 out of fourth place. [Paraskevi Patoulidou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraskevi_Patoulidou "Paraskevi Patoulidou") of Greece won the gold medal to even her own disbelief, dropping to her knees on the track when she realized she had won.
*   [Jennifer Capriati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Capriati "Jennifer Capriati") won the singles tennis competition at the age of 16. She had previously earned a spot in the semifinals of two grand slams at the age of 14.
*   Two gold medals were awarded in solo synchronized swimming after a judge inadvertently entered the score of "8.7" instead of the intended "9.7" in the computerized scoring system for one of [Sylvie Fréchette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvie_Fr%C3%A9chette "Sylvie Fréchette")'s figures. This error ultimately placed Fréchette second, leaving [Kristen Babb-Sprague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Babb-Sprague "Kristen Babb-Sprague") for the gold medal. Following an appeal, [FINA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FINA "FINA") awarded Fréchette a gold medal, replacing her silver medal and leaving the two swimmers both with gold.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-23)
*   Indonesia won its first-ever gold medal after winning a silver at [1988 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics "1988 Summer Olympics"). [Susi Susanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susi_Susanti "Susi Susanti") won the gold in [badminton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badminton "Badminton") women's singles after defeating [Bang Soo-hyun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bang_Soo-hyun "Bang Soo-hyun") in the final round. [Alan Budikusuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Budikusuma "Alan Budikusuma") won the badminton men's singles competition, earning a second gold medal for Indonesia. Several years later, both players married and they received the nickname golden couple or Olympic couple.
